meta.source: Computed by npm run build:data from data/cost-ranges.json, data/installation-costs.json and data/regional-cost-index.json with assets/js/formulas.js
meta.notes: Default result, installed cost tables, state table and cross-checks for the cost calculator.

default.headline: About $1,809 installed
default.explain: 50-gallon gas tank (natural gas, standard vent): the unit itself is about $899 ($749 to $999 in current listings). Installation adds about $910 for labor and 1 extra in the U.S. average (price factor 1.00). Range: $1,249 to $2,599.
default.formula:
Unit (typical) = $899
Labor = $650 × 1.000 = $650
Permit, haul-away and disposal of the old unit = $260 × 1.000 = $260
Total (typical) = $899 + $650 + $260 = $1,809
Low and high use the low and high end of every line the same way.

crossChecks.label: 50-gal gas tank, like-for-like, U.S. average
crossChecks.published: DOE average installed cost $1,432 (2022 dollars, baseline gas storage)
crossChecks.why: Ours is in today’s listing prices; DOE’s is 2022 dollars and averages all sizes from 20 to 55 gallons. PHCC told DOE its RSMeans-based installation costs are too low.
crossChecks.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register: Energy conservation standards for consumer water heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778, May 6, 2024)

crossChecks.label: 50-gal electric tank, like-for-like, U.S. average
crossChecks.published: DOE average installed cost $902 (2022 dollars, baseline electric storage)
crossChecks.why: The largest gap. DOE’s figure is 2022 dollars, includes smaller tanks and many new-construction installs; current 50-gallon listings alone are near $820.
crossChecks.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register: Energy conservation standards for consumer water heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778, May 6, 2024)

crossChecks.label: 50-gal heat pump, replacing an electric tank, U.S. average
crossChecks.published: DOE average installed cost $1,855 (2022 dollars, heat pump level)
crossChecks.why: DOE priced heat pump units from its own cost model for the 2030 market; today’s retail listings are higher. Space work for tight closets is an extra in both.
crossChecks.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register: Energy conservation standards for consumer water heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778, May 6, 2024)

crossChecks.label: Gas tankless replacing a gas tankless, U.S. average
crossChecks.published: DOE average installed cost $2,087 (2023 dollars, baseline gas tankless)
crossChecks.why: Close. Our equipment median is a whole-house unit (8 GPM or more); our labor plus permit ($1,110 typical) matches DOE’s $1,102 installation average.
crossChecks.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register: Energy conservation standards for consumer gas-fired instantaneous water heaters, final rule (89 FR 105188, December 26, 2024)

crossChecks.published: Home Depot data (via This Old House): $1,950 average, $1,600-$5,400 range
crossChecks.why: Industry average, used only as a sanity check: it sits inside our range of common jobs.
crossChecks.source: This Old House (industry range, sanity check only): Water heater installation cost guide (citing The Home Depot data)

rows.label: Permit, haul-away and disposal of the old unit
rows.why: Typical = DOE's $260 for permitting, removal and disposal; industry guides give $25-$300 for the permit and $100-$500 for removal.

rows.label: Thermal expansion tank, parts and labor
rows.why: The tank itself lists for $34-$67 at Home Depot; the rest is about an hour of labor and fittings.

rows.label: Code items: drain pan, seismic straps, relief valve piping
rows.why: A drain pan lists for about $12; strapping and drain work are mostly labor. Which items apply depends on your local code.

rows.label: New or changed venting
rows.why: DOE's earlier estimate was $499 for a non-condensing tankless vent and $263 for a condensing one; industry guides give $300-$1,000.

rows.label: Gas line upgrade or new gas line
rows.why: Industry guides give $275-$1,000; a tankless unit often needs a larger line than the tank it replaces.

rows.label: New 240-volt circuit
rows.why: DOE: "at least several hundred dollars"; industry guides give $300-$800 for electrical work.

rows.label: Electrical panel upgrade (to 200 amps)
rows.why: DOE's range is about $750-$2,000; typical is the middle of that range.

rows.label: Moving the heater to a new spot
rows.why: DOE says relocation can cost up to $2,000; new water, gas or power lines to the new spot are the main cost.

rows.label: Heat pump space work (louvered door, ducting, condensate pump)
rows.why: DOE's adders for the most challenging heat pump installs run $0-$4,000 and average $2,000.

extras.source: Hot Water Math installation cost ranges, anchored to the U.S. Department of Energy's 2024 consumer water heater rules (installation costs built from RSMeans) and Home Depot listing prices, and checked against published industry ranges

labor.caption: Installation labor by type, like-for-like (U.S. average)

rows.label: Gas tank (standard vent)
rows.why: DOE's average installed cost for a standard gas tank ($1,432 in 2022 dollars, equipment included) leaves several hundred dollars for installation; industry guides give $150-$800 labor.

rows.label: Electric tank
rows.why: No vent or gas connection, so less work than gas; DOE's electric average ($902 installed, 2022 dollars) is its lowest of all types.

rows.label: Heat pump (hybrid), 240 V
rows.why: A heavier, taller unit plus a condensate drain. Extra work for tight spaces is a separate extra, as in DOE's analysis.

rows.label: Gas tankless
rows.why: DOE's average installation cost is $1,102 (non-condensing) and $1,025 (condensing), including about $260 for permit, removal and disposal, which we list separately; industry guides give $800-$1,500 labor.

rows.label: Electric tankless
rows.why: Wall mounting and wiring to existing circuits; new circuits or a panel upgrade are extras. DOE did not analyze electric tankless units.
